## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cakkhu Sutta* (“The Eye”, Iti 61; PTS It 52) is a discourse in the *Tikanipāta* (Book of the Threes) of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta presents a concise threefold classification of eyes: the physical eye of flesh (*maṁsacakkhu*), the clairvoyant divine eye (*dibbacakkhu*), and the eye of discernment or wisdom (*paññācakkhu*) [SuttaCentral; Vasubandhu 1991].
This canonical triad is cited and examined across later Buddhist scholastic traditions. In the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya*, Vasubandhu records an opinion defining visible matter (*rūpāyatana*) as the objective sphere of three kinds of eyes—the fleshy, divine, and wisdom eyes (*māṁsa-*, *divya-*, and *prajñācakṣus*)—specifically citing sutta 61 of the *Itivuttaka* [Vasubandhu 1991]. In Theravāda literature, SuttaCentral notes references to the sutta in the *Kathāvatthu* (*Dibbacakkhukathā*, Kv 3.7) and the *Milindapañha* (*Sivirājacakkhudānapañha*, Mil 5.1.5) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse computations from DharmaNexus strongly corroborate the relationship with the *Kathāvatthu*, identifying 8 shared passages (974 characters) with Kv 3.7, notably aligning segments §2.1–4.6 of the sutta with §13.4–15.6 of Kv 3.7 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies shared phrasing between Iti 61 and ten other *Itivuttaka* discourses (most extensively Iti 64, Iti 66, Iti 67, and Iti 60), representing the standard structural and opening formulas common to discourses in the collection [DharmaNexus].
